labeling.method: All 50 cases passed structural validation. The labels were compared with 39 existing context-relevance labels across the 13-case calibration set; all six disagreements were inspected against the chunks and claim-level calibration evidence. Zero- and high-relevance-count outliers were inspected. One non-atomic lifespan claim was split and its affected judgments corrected. The project owner previously authorized Codex-reviewed labels for this straightforward documentation corpus.
labeling.usage: Silver project labels for controlled retrieval experiments. They are AI-generated and Codex-reviewed, not human-authored gold labels or an external benchmark.

audit.outlier_review: Inspected the sole zero-relevance case and every case with at most two or at least seventeen relevant candidates. Counts were consistent with retrieval misses or duplicate evidence across chunking strategies.
audit.known_limitation: The review was targeted rather than a human verification of every individual judgment. Three remaining differences from calibration context-precision labels agree with the same calibration set's stricter claim-level context-recall evidence.

case_overrides.rationale: The proposal combined on_event deprecation and lifespan/event-handler exclusivity into one claim. They are independently supportable facts; the three semantic baseline chunks support deprecation but not exclusivity.

reference_claims.claim: The lifespan parameter accepts an async context manager.
Code before yield runs once at startup before requests are received.
Code after yield runs once at shutdown after requests have been handled.
Lifespan is useful for shared resources such as machine learning models and database connection pools.
Lifespan avoids loading expensive shared resources at module import during independent tests.
on_event startup and shutdown handlers are deprecated.
When lifespan is supplied, on_event handlers are not called and the two mechanisms cannot be mixed.
Lifespan events apply only to the main application and not mounted sub-applications.
